about: Which example-library entries would genuinely help write the CadQuery code for each benchmark request (eval/cases.json), used by eval/retrieval.py to score retrieval. Drafted by Claude for review: 'reviewed' says whether a human has checked them. An empty list means nothing in the library is relevant, so the ideal retriever returns nothing above its cutoff.

s01.why: spacer = tube: same outer/inner diameter cylinder as the washer

s02.why: box primitive plus a drilled through hole

s03.why: regular polygon extrude; hex nut shows across-flats sizing

s05.why: a cone is a revolved profile (or a loft to a point)

m01.why: rectangular hole grid, plate with holes, rounded vertical edges

m04.why: bolt-circle holes on a disc; centre hole like a washer

m05.why: evenly spaced repeated cuts along a bar

m06.why: extruded cross-section profile; thin walls; L/U-shaped section

m07.why: cylindrical shell open at the top; edge fillet

h02.why: plate leaning at an angle on a base; side-profile extrude

h03.why: curved arm swept along an arc; countersunk screw holes

p02.why: cube body, softened edges, symbols cut into faces

p03.why: organic shapes: nothing in the library helps; should be declined
